about: The whole history of Nvidia. Long-form 16:9 stickman history, episode 3 of Tech, explained (first of the weekly 'whole history' series). Chatterbox voice, the long-form voice Isac picked on 2026-10-24, levelled per line, one global speed.

lines.text: Type one question into ChatGPT tonight.
Before the first word comes back, your question lands in a building full of chips, all doing math at the same time.
Most of the world's AI chips come from one company.
A company that started in a Denny's, making chips for video games.
Nvidia isn't an AI company that used to make gaming chips.
It's a gaming company whose math turned out to be the math of AI.
And the size of it breaks your brain.
When Nvidia went public in 1999, it raised about 42 million dollars.
lines.say: When Nvidia went public in nineteen ninety-nine, it raised about forty-two million dollars.

lines.text: Today, it takes in that much money in less than an hour.
It's worth about 5 trillion dollars, the most valuable company on Earth.
lines.say: It's worth about five trillion dollars, the most valuable company on Earth.

lines.text: And the man who runs it once cleaned toilets at a school for troubled kids.
Here's what should be impossible.
In the nineties, dozens of companies were making graphics chips.
Nvidia's first chip flopped. It came within weeks of running out of money.
The king of the industry was a company called 3dfx. Nvidia ended up buying what was left of it.
lines.say: The king of the industry was a company called three D F X. Nvidia ended up buying what was left of it.

lines.text: So how did a chip for video games end up running AI?
Why did Wall Street hate the bet that made it rich?
And can anything knock it off the top?
This is the story of a booth at Denny's, a name a toilet paper company got to first, a rescue from Sega,
and two gaming cards at a student's house that changed computers forever.
The whole history of Nvidia.
It starts in 1973, when a nine-year-old named Jensen Huang is sent from Taiwan to America.
lines.say: It starts in nineteen seventy-three, when a nine-year-old named Jensen Huang is sent from Taiwan to America.

lines.text: His relatives enroll him at what they think is a fancy boarding school in Kentucky.
It's actually a school for troubled kids. His job is cleaning the toilets. Every day.
His roommate is seventeen, covered in tattoos, and can't read.
So Jensen teaches him to read, and the roommate teaches Jensen to bench press.
At fifteen, he gets a job at a Denny's in Oregon. Washing dishes, then bussing tables, then waiting them.
Remember Denny's. It comes back.
He studies electrical engineering, and by his late twenties he's designing chips in Silicon Valley.
In late 1992, he sits down with two engineers, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, at a Denny's in San Jose.
lines.say: In late nineteen ninety-two, he sits down with two engineers, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, at a Denny's in San Jose.

lines.text: Coffee, eggs, hours of talking. The plan: a chip that makes video games look real.
In April 1993, they start the company with about 40 thousand dollars.
lines.say: In April nineteen ninety-three, they start the company with about forty thousand dollars.

lines.text: They don't have a name yet, so they label their files NV, for next version.
lines.say: They don't have a name yet, so they label their files N V, for next version.

lines.text: They want to call it NVision. But a toilet paper company already has it.
lines.say: They want to call it En-vision. But a toilet paper company already has it.

lines.text: So Jensen picks a word with an N and a V: invidia, Latin for envy.
Then he pitches his old boss, who calls it one of the worst pitches he's ever heard, and phones a famous investor anyway.
That investor, Don Valentine of Sequoia, puts money in, with a warning.
If you lose my money, I will kill you.
In 1995, Nvidia's first chip comes out. It's called NV1, and it builds 3D worlds out of curves.
lines.say: In nineteen ninety-five, Nvidia's first chip comes out. It's called N V one, and it builds 3D worlds out of curves.

lines.text: Everyone else picks triangles. And when Microsoft builds its game graphics around triangles too, the curve bet is dead.
Nvidia is also building a chip for Sega's next console, the same wrong way.
So Jensen does something wild. He tells Sega to find another partner, and asks them to pay Nvidia anyway.
Sega's American boss, Shoichiro Irimajiri, says yes. 5 million dollars. Enough to stay alive for about six months.
lines.say: Sega's American boss, Shoichiro Irimajiri, says yes. Five million dollars. Enough to stay alive for about six months.

lines.text: Nvidia lays off about half its people and bets everything on one chip that draws triangles, the RIVA 128.
lines.say: Nvidia lays off about half its people and bets everything on one chip that draws triangles, the Riva one twenty-eight.

lines.text: It ships in August 1997, with about one month of payroll left in the bank.
lines.say: It ships in August nineteen ninety-seven, with about one month of payroll left in the bank.

lines.text: It sells about a million units in four months.
And one sentence becomes the company's unofficial motto.
Our company is thirty days from going out of business.
On January 22nd, 1999, Nvidia goes public at 12 dollars a share. Remember that 12 dollars.
lines.say: On January twenty-second, nineteen ninety-nine, Nvidia goes public at twelve dollars a share. Remember that twelve dollars.

lines.text: That same year it launches the GeForce 256, and sells it with a brand new word: the world's first GPU.
lines.say: That same year it launches the GeForce two fifty-six, and sells it with a brand new word: the world's first G P U.

lines.text: So what is a GPU, actually?
lines.say: So what is a G P U, actually?

lines.text: To draw one frame of a game on an HD screen, you color about two million pixels. Then you do it again, sixty times a second.
A normal processor, a CPU, is like a few brilliant professors. They can solve anything, but one problem at a time.
lines.say: A normal processor, a C P U, is like a few brilliant professors. They can solve anything, but one problem at a time.

lines.text: A GPU is a stadium full of kids who can only do simple sums. But they all do them at the same moment.
lines.say: A G P U is a stadium full of kids who can only do simple sums. But they all do them at the same moment.

lines.text: One kid adds a little red to this pixel. Another darkens that one. Two million kids, one sum each, done.
For coloring pixels, the stadium wins. Every time.
In 2000, Nvidia agrees to buy the remains of 3dfx, the company that used to rule gaming graphics.
lines.say: In two thousand, Nvidia agrees to buy the remains of three D F X, the company that used to rule gaming graphics.

lines.text: Then Microsoft picks Nvidia for the graphics in its first Xbox, and pays 200 million dollars up front.
lines.say: Then Microsoft picks Nvidia for the graphics in its first Xbox, and pays two hundred million dollars up front.

lines.text: And when the stock hits 100 dollars, Jensen gets the company logo tattooed on his body.
lines.say: And when the stock hits a hundred dollars, Jensen gets the company logo tattooed on his body.

lines.text: Meanwhile, at Stanford, a grad student named Ian Buck is wiring GeForce cards together.
He builds a language that lets them do math that has nothing to do with games. Nvidia hires him in 2004.
lines.say: He builds a language that lets them do math that has nothing to do with games. Nvidia hires him in two thousand four.

lines.text: In 2006, Nvidia announces CUDA. It turns that stadium of kids loose on any problem: weather, medicine, physics.
lines.say: In two thousand six, Nvidia announces Cuda. It turns that stadium of kids loose on any problem: weather, medicine, physics.

lines.text: And it builds CUDA into its ordinary gaming chips. Millions of gamers carry a supercomputer feature they will never use.
lines.say: And it builds Cuda into its ordinary gaming chips. Millions of gamers carry a supercomputer feature they will never use.

lines.text: The idea: put the tool in millions of computers first, and the people who need it will find it.
Wall Street sees the bill, not the point.
In 2008, Nvidia takes a charge of about 200 million dollars for faulty laptop chips, and the stock falls 31 percent in one day.
lines.say: In two thousand eight, Nvidia takes a charge of about two hundred million dollars for faulty laptop chips, and the stock falls thirty-one percent in one day.

lines.text: By the end of that year, it has lost about three quarters of its value.
Remember thirty days from dead? This time, Nvidia keeps paying for CUDA anyway.
lines.say: Remember thirty days from dead? This time, Nvidia keeps paying for Cuda anyway.

lines.text: A tool for a market that doesn't exist yet.
Then, in 2012, the market finally shows up, at a student's parents' house.
lines.say: Then, in twenty twelve, the market finally shows up, at a student's parents' house.

lines.text: Alex Krizhevsky, his friend Ilya Sutskever and their professor Geoffrey Hinton want to teach a computer to recognize pictures.
They train a neural network on two Nvidia gaming cards, GTX 580s, for about a week.
lines.say: They train a neural network on two Nvidia gaming cards, G T X five-eighties, for about a week.

lines.text: It enters the biggest image contest in the world and wins by a mile: about 15 percent wrong, when the next best was 26.
lines.say: It enters the biggest image contest in the world and wins by a mile: about fifteen percent wrong, when the next best was twenty-six.

lines.text: The math inside a neural network is the same kind of simple sums as coloring pixels. Millions of them, all at once.
The stadium of kids was built for games. It was perfect for AI.
You may have heard Nvidia just got lucky with AI. Partly true. But luck only pays if you're already standing there.
Jensen goes all in. In 2016, he hand-delivers the first DGX-1, an AI computer, to a small lab in San Francisco called OpenAI.
lines.say: Jensen goes all in. In twenty sixteen, he hand-delivers the first D G X one, an AI computer, to a small lab in San Francisco called OpenAI.

lines.text: He signs it: to the future of computing and humanity.
One of OpenAI's founders is Ilya Sutskever. From the student's house.
Then crypto miners buy up gaming cards, crypto crashes in 2018, and Nvidia's stock loses more than half its value in months.
lines.say: Then crypto miners buy up gaming cards, crypto crashes in twenty eighteen, and Nvidia's stock loses more than half its value in months.

lines.text: Regulators later fine it 5.5 million dollars for not telling investors how much crypto was behind its sales.
lines.say: Regulators later fine it five and a half million dollars for not telling investors how much crypto was behind its sales.

lines.text: On November 30th, 2022, OpenAI releases ChatGPT.
lines.say: On November thirtieth, twenty twenty-two, OpenAI releases ChatGPT.

lines.text: It was trained on a Microsoft supercomputer built from tens of thousands of Nvidia chips.
Suddenly every tech giant on Earth wants the same thing, and only one company really sells it.
In a gold rush, sell shovels.
Nvidia's top AI chip, the H100, sells for tens of thousands of dollars each, and buyers wait months to get one.
lines.say: Nvidia's top AI chip, the H one hundred, sells for tens of thousands of dollars each, and buyers wait months to get one.

lines.text: In May 2023, Nvidia is worth a trillion dollars. Denny's puts a plaque on the booth: the booth that launched a 1 trillion dollar company.
lines.say: In May twenty twenty-three, Nvidia is worth a trillion dollars. Denny's puts a plaque on the booth: the booth that launched a one trillion dollar company.

lines.text: In June 2024, it passes Microsoft and Apple to become the most valuable company in the world.
lines.say: In June twenty twenty-four, it passes Microsoft and Apple to become the most valuable company in the world.

lines.text: Then, in January 2025, a Chinese lab called DeepSeek shows off a cheap AI model, and Nvidia loses about 589 billion dollars of value in one day.
lines.say: Then, in January twenty twenty-five, a Chinese lab called DeepSeek shows off a cheap AI model, and Nvidia loses about five hundred eighty-nine billion dollars of value in one day.

lines.text: The biggest one-day loss in stock market history.
And then it just keeps climbing. 4 trillion in July 2025. 5 trillion that October. The first company ever to reach either one.
lines.say: And then it just keeps climbing. Four trillion in July twenty twenty-five. Five trillion that October. The first company ever to reach either one.

lines.text: Which brings us to right now. October 2026.
lines.say: Which brings us to right now. October twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: In its last quarter, Nvidia brought in 96.2 billion dollars. Data centers alone were 89 billion.
lines.say: In its last quarter, Nvidia brought in ninety-six point two billion dollars. Data centers alone were eighty-nine billion.

lines.text: That's more than nine of every ten dollars. The gaming company now mostly sells to AI.
Its newest chips, Vera Rubin, are in full production, and it expects 108 billion this quarter, without counting any AI chip sales to China.
lines.say: Its newest chips, Vera Rubin, are in full production, and it expects a hundred and eight billion this quarter, without counting any AI chip sales to China.

lines.text: But it's not a straight line. On October 6th the stock hit a record, then chip stocks fell eight days in a row, their longest streak since 2008.
lines.say: But it's not a straight line. On October sixth the stock hit a record, then chip stocks fell eight days in a row, their longest streak since two thousand eight.

lines.text: Today, Nvidia is worth about 5.2 trillion dollars.
lines.say: Today, Nvidia is worth about five point two trillion dollars.

lines.text: And remember that 12 dollar share from 1999? After six stock splits, it's 480 shares, worth about 104 thousand dollars.
lines.say: And remember that twelve dollar share from nineteen ninety-nine? After six stock splits, it's four hundred eighty shares, worth about a hundred and four thousand dollars.

lines.text: Jensen Huang is still the CEO, thirty-three years later. Still in the leather jacket.
The kid who cleaned toilets in Kentucky is now worth more than 200 billion dollars.
lines.say: The kid who cleaned toilets in Kentucky is now worth more than two hundred billion dollars.

lines.text: He once said that if he could go back, he wouldn't start Nvidia again. It was a million times harder than he expected.
So why does any of this matter?
Because the chips answering your questions are cousins of the chips drawing your video games.
For twenty years, gamers paid for the machine that AI would need.
Nvidia didn't predict AI. It built a stadium for games, kept paying for it when nobody cared, and was standing there when AI walked in.
And now Google, Amazon and AMD are all building chips to knock Nvidia off the top.
In 1993, three engineers drank a lot of coffee at a Denny's.
lines.say: In nineteen ninety-three, three engineers drank a lot of coffee at a Denny's.

lines.text: Tonight, someone in that same diner can type a question into ChatGPT, and the answer will most likely run on their chips.
